faqs.question: What is the ACQUITY UPLC M-Class System used for?
faqs.answer: It's a nano- to microscale UPLC system for sample-limited LC-MS work, used primarily in proteomics, biomarker discovery, protein conformation analysis, and other applications where sample material is severely limited.

faqs.question: What flow rate range does M-Class cover?
faqs.answer: 200 nL/min to 100 µL/min, delivered without flow splitting.

faqs.question: Why does flow splitting matter?
faqs.answer: Splitting produces low flow by diverting most of an analytical pump's output, which makes the flow reaching the column dependent on restrictor and back pressure conditions. Direct, non-split delivery with pulse-less flow control gives increased retention time reproducibility instead.

faqs.question: What column inner diameters does the system support?
faqs.answer: Waters' body copy states 75 µm to 1.0 mm and the specification table states 75 µm to 4.6 mm. Confirm the exact range against the intended column set at configuration.

faqs.question: Can optical detection be used at all column sizes?
faqs.answer: Mass spectrometry supports the full column inner diameter range; optical detection applies to 300 µm to 1 mm I.D. columns.

faqs.question: Why does low flow increase sensitivity?
faqs.answer: Delivering the same quantity of analyte in less volume raises concentration at the source, improving sensitivity for any mass spectrometer without changing the instrument.

faqs.question: What is the sample flow path made from?
faqs.answer: The flow path is non-ferrous, with non-reactive surfaces maintaining sample integrity through the system.

faqs.question: What is the HDX Technology configuration for?
faqs.answer: Quantifying small changes in protein conformation, with an extended pressure range for higher efficiency separation and DynamX HDX Data Analysis Software integrating sample prep through sequence determination, D2 uptake curves, and comparison plots.

faqs.question: What is the 2D Technology configuration for?
faqs.answer: Expanding dynamic range and throughput through reversed-phase/reversed-phase 2D-LC, running the first dimension at pH 10 and the second at pH 2 with MS-compatible eluents.

faqs.question: What injection volumes does the system accept?
faqs.answer: 0.1 µL to 100.0 µL.

faqs.question: Does M-Class include column tracking?
faqs.answer: No. Column tracking is not provided on this system, unlike the analytical-scale ACQUITY systems that carry eCord Technology.

faqs.question: What is the operating pH range?
faqs.answer: 2 to 10 — narrower than the analytical-scale ACQUITY systems, which is worth checking against the intended mobile phase chemistry.

faqs.question: What software controls the system?
faqs.answer: MassLynx Software per the specification, with new drivers integrating the system into existing MassLynx workflows. Waters also publishes Empower and third-party driver pack certificates for the platform, so confirm the software scope at configuration.

faqs.question: What is the maximum sample capacity?
faqs.answer: Up to 21 plates with the Sample Organizer.

faqs.question: How much bench space does the system need?
faqs.answer: 34.3 cm wide, 69.7 cm high, and 71.2 cm deep in the µBSM, µSM-FL, TVM configuration.

longForm.heroLead: The usual route to nanoflow is splitting an analytical-scale pump's output down. It works, and it costs reproducibility and reliability — which is precisely the trade-off that stops labs from adopting low-flow LC-MS despite the sensitivity waiting on the other side. ACQUITY UPLC M-Class delivers 200 nL/min through 100 µL/min directly, without splitting. Automatic solvent flow control algorithms provide pulse-less flow, and retention time reproducibility follows from that rather than being fought for. Every part of the system was designed and tested to deliver the right flow for the right column, across inner diameters from 75 µm upward. For samples that are severely limited in amount or availability, that combination is the whole argument: higher sensitivity from any mass spectrometer, less sample volume consumed, increased dynamic range, and non-reactive surfaces that keep the sample intact on the way to the source.

faqs.question: What is the ACQUITY UPLC I-Class PLUS System used for?
faqs.answer: It's a high-performance binary UPLC system built for maximum resolution and sensitivity, used particularly as an LC-MS front end in bioanalysis, impurity profiling, peptide characterization, and clinical research.

faqs.question: What is system band spread and why does 4 µL matter?
faqs.answer: System band spread is how much the flow path broadens a peak after the column has separated it. Waters compared a tetracaine impurity analysis on I-Class PLUS at 4 µL against a UHPLC system at 20 µL under identical conditions, achieving significantly better resolution on I-Class PLUS.

faqs.question: What is the maximum operating pressure?
faqs.answer: 18,000 psi, the highest in the ACQUITY UPLC PLUS Series, with a flow rate range up to 2.0 mL/min.

faqs.question: What is the sample carryover specification?
faqs.answer: Below 0.001% for caffeine under UV conditions, and manageable through programmable method settings for compatibility with the most sensitive mass spectrometers.

faqs.question: Why is I-Class PLUS recommended as a mass spectrometry inlet?
faqs.answer: Narrow peak widths improve both resolution and ionization efficiency, enhancing MS sensitivity, while high resolution minimizes interference from co-elutions and industry-leading carryover protects trace-level detection.

faqs.question: How many columns can the system hold?
faqs.answer: Up to two columns of 150 mm length and up to 4.6 mm internal diameter, with accurate temperature control across the entire column and active preheating.

faqs.question: What pump configuration does I-Class PLUS use?
faqs.answer: A Binary Solvent Manager delivering precise, accurate blending for up to four solvents with an integrated solvent-select valve.

faqs.question: What injector options are available?
faqs.answer: Flow-through needle and fixed loop, giving sample injection versatility depending on the application.

faqs.question: What are CORTECS columns and why pair them with this system?
faqs.answer: CORTECS 1.6 µm solid-core columns deliver exceptional efficiency and narrower peaks; paired with the system's ultra-low dispersion and 18,000 psi headroom, they produce higher peak capacity for the toughest samples.

faqs.question: How is I-Class PLUS different from H-Class PLUS?
faqs.answer: I-Class PLUS offers higher pressure (18,000 versus 15,000 psi) and lower carryover with the lowest dispersion in the series, but takes two columns and is binary only. H-Class PLUS offers up to six columns, nine-solvent quaternary blending, and automated method screening.

faqs.question: Does the system support annual qualification?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Waters Empower-based automated System Qualification Tool (SQT) minimizes the time and cost associated with annual qualification.

faqs.question: What software controls the system?
faqs.answer: Empower, MassLynx, waters_connect, the UNIFI Scientific Information System, and several third-party software packages.

faqs.question: Does the system handle metal-sensitive analytes?
faqs.answer: The sample flow path is stainless steel, so metal-sensitive analytes may require passivation. Where that's a recurring issue, the ACQUITY Premier System's inert MaxPeak HPS flow path is designed for exactly that problem.

faqs.question: What is multidimensional UPLC?
faqs.answer: A configuration allowing selective isolation across more than one separation dimension, improving characterization where a single dimension cannot resolve everything of interest.

faqs.question: What is the maximum sample capacity?
faqs.answer: Up to 20 plates with the Sample Organizer.

faqs.question: How much bench space does the system need?
faqs.answer: 34.3 cm wide, 71.1 cm high, and 71.2 cm deep in the QSM or BSM, SM-FTN, CHA configuration.

faqs.question: What is the ACQUITY UPLC H-Class PLUS System used for?
faqs.answer: It's a UPLC system for method development and routine analysis, built to decrease time to result while increasing the depth and quality of information from sample analysis.

faqs.question: How much can scaling a method to UPLC save?
faqs.answer: Waters scaled the USP analysis of diclazuril and organic impurities from HPLC to UPLC, achieving a 4× reduction in run time and a 10× reduction in solvent consumption.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the Quaternary and Binary configurations?
faqs.answer: Quaternary blends up to nine solvents and automatically screens column and eluent combinations, built for method development. Binary offers the lowest system volume with high-pressure mixing, built for reproducible routine LC-MS.

faqs.question: Why does low dispersion matter if the system already runs at 15,000 psi?
faqs.answer: High pressure alone doesn't produce sharp peaks. System dispersion has to be matched to the narrow peak widths that sub-2 µm columns generate, or the resolution the chemistry provides is lost in the system.

faqs.question: What is Auto•Blend Plus Technology?
faqs.answer: It automates mobile phase formulation and allows pH and ionic strength to be screened as method parameters, significantly reducing time spent preparing mobile phases in the prep lab.

faqs.question: How many columns can be screened at once?
faqs.answer: Up to six columns of 150 mm length and up to 4.6 mm internal diameter, in independently temperature-controlled compartments with active preheating.

faqs.question: How many solvents can the system blend?
faqs.answer: Up to nine on the Quaternary Solvent Manager with the integrated solvent-select valve, or up to four on the Binary Solvent Manager.

faqs.question: Can methods be transferred from another LC system?
faqs.answer: Yes. Gradient SmartStart adjusts for system volume differences when transferring from an alternative LC system, without altering the method table.

faqs.question: What is the maximum operating pressure and flow rate?
faqs.answer: 15,000 psi, with an operating flow rate range up to 2.2 mL/min.

faqs.question: Which columns does the system support?
faqs.answer: Any analytical LC column, with particle sizes from sub-2 µm to 5 µm.

faqs.question: What is the sample carryover specification?
faqs.answer: ≤0.002% for caffeine under UV conditions, with direct inject sampling using a needle-in-flow-path design for an accurate seal at high pressure.

faqs.question: Does H-Class PLUS work with mass spectrometry?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Binary configuration is built for reproducible everyday LC-MS with any tandem quad or Q-ToF, and pairs with Waters tandem quadrupole technology for routine quantitative UPLC-MS/MS.

faqs.question: Does the system need passivation for metal-sensitive analytes?
faqs.answer: The sample flow path is stainless steel, so metal-sensitive analytes may require passivation. Where that's a recurring problem, the ACQUITY Premier System's inert MaxPeak HPS flow path is designed to remove the need entirely.

faqs.question: What software controls the system?
faqs.answer: Empower, MassLynx, waters_connect, the UNIFI Scientific Information System, and several third-party software packages.

faqs.question: What is the maximum sample capacity?
faqs.answer: Up to 20 plates with the Sample Organizer.

faqs.question: How much bench space does the system need?
faqs.answer: 34.3 cm wide, 71.1 cm high, and 71.2 cm deep in the QSM or BSM, SM-FTN, CHA configuration.

items: High pressure and UPLC performance are not the same thing. A system rated to 15,000 psi can still produce broad peaks if its extra-column dispersion is wider than the peaks the column is generating.
True UPLC requires system dispersion matched to the peak widths associated with narrow-bore columns packed with sub-2 µm particles — that matching is the design premise here.

Waters showed the difference directly: the same method, the same column, run on a low-dispersion H-Class PLUS versus a higher-dispersion UHPLC system, with the resolution difference visible in the chromatogram.

The productivity case is quantified. Scaling the USP diclazuril and organic impurity analysis from HPLC through UHPLC to UPLC gave a 4× reduction in run time and a 10× reduction in solvent consumption.
Those two numbers move different budget lines: run time reduction increases sample throughput per instrument, solvent reduction cuts consumables spend and waste disposal cost per analysis.
Existing HPLC methods run on the system now, so the transition is gradual rather than a cliff — the lab keeps its validated work while modernizing selectively.
A separate transfer example showed analysis time going from 5 minutes to 3 through direct transfer without gradient delay, a 40% runtime reduction.
Gradient SmartStart handles system volume differences when methods arrive from another LC platform, without requiring the method table to be altered.

longForm.heroHook: The peak you couldn't see wasn't absent. It was stuck to the flow path.
longForm.heroLead: Metal-sensitive compounds — phosphopeptides, nucleotides, organic acids, chelators — adsorb onto stainless steel surfaces inside a conventional LC. The result is broad peaks, large RSDs, and analytes that go undetected entirely. The usual remedy is passivation: hours of system conditioning before a run, repeated whenever the system sits idle. ACQUITY Premier removes the cause. MaxPeak High Performance Surfaces Technology makes the sample flow path inert, so metal-sensitive analytes stay in the mobile phase instead of binding to the hardware. Waters measured a 54% reduction in peak tailing on a deamidation impurity peptide, and reduced adsorption of a doubly phosphorylated insulin receptor peptide against conventional LC technology. The chromatography underneath is true UPLC — 15,000 psi, ultra-low dispersion, high resolution, on the ACQUITY UPLC PLUS Series platform. And with passivation eliminated, the first injection is usable rather than being the first of several conditioning runs.

body.title: Advanced Performance LC System
body.text: Builds on the reliability, ruggedness and configuration flexibility of the ACQUITY UPLC H Class PLUS and I Class PLUS systems.

body.title: MaxPeak HPS Technology
body.text: Provides an inert sample flow path designed to reduce interactions between metal sensitive analytes and system surfaces, improving separation and detection.

body.title: Reduced analyte adsorption
body.text: Helps minimize non specific adsorption that can cause peak broadening, tailing, variable results and analyte loss.

body.title: Improved peak shape
body.text: Waters reports a 54% reduction in peak tailing for T37 peptide analysis, supporting improved detection of deamidation impurities.

body.title: Improved detection of metal sensitive compounds
body.text: Demonstrated reduced adsorption for phosphorylated peptides and improved peak area and peak shape for dexamethasone sodium phosphate.

body.title: First injection performance
body.text: Designed to provide reproducible performance from the first injection, reducing the need for time consuming system and column passivation.

body.title: High pressure operation
body.text: Supports pressures up to 15,000 psi across a flow rate range of 0.001 to 2.000 mL/min.

body.title: Wide operating pH range
body.text: Supports an operating pH range of 1 to 12.5.

body.title: Binary and Quaternary configurations
body.text: Available with both binary and quaternary pump options to suit different LC workflows.

body.title: Controlled solvent conditioning
body.text: Active preheating is provided as standard for consistent solvent conditioning.

body.title: Flexible injection options
body.text: Supports flow through needle and fixed loop injection, along with direct inject sampling for high precision applications.

body.title: Low carryover
body.text: Provides sample carryover of ≤0.002%, supporting sensitive analytical workflows.

body.title: Controlled sample temperature
body.text: The sample compartment operates from 4 to 40 °C.

body.title: Flexible column capacity
body.text: Supports up to six columns with lengths up to 150 mm and internal diameters up to 4.6 mm.

body.title: eCord column tracking
body.text: Tracks and archives column usage to support method management and column history.

body.title: High sample capacity
body.text: The Sample Organizer supports up to 8,064 samples.

body.title: Multiple detection options
body.text: Compatible with TUV, PDA eλ, FLR, charged aerosol, refractive index, evaporative light scattering and mass spectrometer detection.

body.title: Designed for metal sensitive analytes
body.text: The ACQUITY Premier System and ACQUITY Premier Columns are designed together to reduce analyte losses and improve repeatability.

body.title: LC MS compatibility
body.text: When paired with a Waters mass spectrometer, the system supports identification and quantification of unknown compounds and detection of trace components in complex samples.

body.title: Sustainable system design
body.text: The system carries an ACT label and incorporates renewable powered manufacturing, recycled content, responsible chemical management and sustainable packaging.
